subject: shotgun
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: shotgun, in the place of the game's models/v_shotgun.mdl, models/p_shotgun.mdl, models/w_shotgun.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_9mmar.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, A, A, A where the asset was C, B, A, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words the outline is right: one long shape with a barrel, a tube under it, a receiver, a ribbed pump in the middle, and a stock whose end curls over. The hook shows in front-left, front-right and below, and no part sticks out or is missing in the six sides. The stock's folding joint is not clear enough to read here (see M3), but the silhouette itself is not wrong.

M2.reason: Length is 28.2 against the 30 asked, 6% short, within the 15% band. The width (17.1) and height (3.8) are not in the brief, so they are not scored against it.

M3.reason: Small parts checked against the brief's list. Present and readable: the barrel, a tube magazine under it (two parallel tubes in front-right), the pump with its ribs (first-person, left), the receiver with an ejection port (first-person), a front bead at the muzzle (top view, first-person), and the hooked stock end (below, front-left, front-right). Not readable at this scale: the folding stock's hinge, which the brief asks for; the pump's round sides cannot be counted; and the trigger and guard, which do not show in the grip-free views. A missing small part caps this at 1.

M4.reason: Black metal throughout, with the pump dark grey, as the brief allows for a dark pump. Highlights on the barrel and receiver are metal sheen, not a different material. No region reads as a wrong colour.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings. The pump ribs, the ejection port and the receiver panel lines are there and add nothing wrong. Shading is low-resolution and blocky, but nothing the brief names is smeared or missing.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up rule: the asset was picked as the one not made by Valve in only 1 of 4 readings (picked at chance). Note for the record: in first-person.png the asset (left) and the game's own (right) look alike to the eye in outline, pump and placement, so a player might take it for the original. Steven should look at that before this is called original.

M7.reason: In the world views the weapon lies flat on its side with its long axis along the ground, as a world weapon should, with the muzzle at one end and the stock hook at the other. In first-person it is upright with the muzzle up and forward. Nothing is upside down or floating in the sides.

M8.reason: checkErrors is empty. 174 triangles is under twice the median of Half-Life's shotguns (2 x 138 = 276) and under the third quartile (187), so within the band. Nothing visibly open except the bore at the muzzle (normal for a barrel the player sees) and a lit hollow at the stock's end seen from behind, which reads as the hook's inside and not a hole in a face the game shows. No floating part in the views.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset sits where the game's own sits: same height and angle at the lower right of the frame, same way round (muzzle up and forward), with the orange glove holding the grip at the same place as in the game's frame. In attack.png the weapon moves with the hand through its shots (frames 0/20 to 20/20): the hand stays under the grip in every frame, and the weapon leaves the picture at the bottom in some frames, which is not it leaving the hands.
